retrocomputers.ponder.tag.computers.desc: From raw materials to a working terminal
retrocomputers.ponder.first_computer.tex: This is the computer chassis. To make it in survival, start with the Mining and processing ores guide, then follow the board and equipment guides.
In JEI, hover over an item and press R to see how to make it. In Creative, find the blocks and parts in the Retro Computers tab.
Place the chassis. Hold a basic CPU, then right-click the chassis. Repeat with basic RAM, a cassette drive and a 12 FE/t power supply.
Put an Alternator against the chassis. Connect a spinning Create shaft to the Alternator and reach 32 RPM. The power setup guide shows the details.
Place one monitor with its green face toward you. Place the keyboard where you can use it while looking at that screen.
Hold the Linking Probe and right-click the chassis first. A message confirms the computer is selected.
With the same probe, right-click the monitor and then the keyboard. The powered monitor shows READY. TYPE HELP.
Open the keyboard. On the first boot enter a name, such as lab, and press RETURN. Then type HELP to list the commands.
retrocomputers.ponder.mining.text_1: Find silicon in stone at Y 0–96 in new Overworld chunks. Mine it with an iron pickaxe or better.
retrocomputers.ponder.mining.text_2: Tin forms in stone at Y 0–64. Use an iron pickaxe or better here as well.
retrocomputers.ponder.mining.text_3: Feed raw tin or raw silicon between rotating Crushing Wheels to get two pieces of crushed ore.
retrocomputers.ponder.mining.text_4: Blow air from an Encased Fan through water onto the crushed ore. Bulk washing turns it into clean dust.
retrocomputers.ponder.mining.text_5: Smelt tin dust into tin ingots.
retrocomputers.ponder.boards.text_1: Heat a Basin and mix silicon dust, clay and quartz for ceramic. Mix tin and copper ingots in the heated Basin for solder.
retrocomputers.ponder.boards.text_2: Mix dried kelp, paper and clay in the heated Basin for resin. Use a saw to make copper traces from a copper sheet.
retrocomputers.ponder.parts.text_1: Start each basic part from a circuit board. The first Deployer selects the line: wafer for CPU, redstone for RAM, tape for the drive, ferrite for power.
retrocomputers.ponder.parts.text_2: A heated Mixer makes magnetic tape from resin, paper and an iron nugget. A Press compacts two iron nuggets and redstone into ferrite cores.
retrocomputers.ponder.parts.text_3: Hover over the finished part in JEI and press R. Follow the machines in order; the item stays unfinished until both loops are complete.
retrocomputers.ponder.parts.text_4: Upgrades start with the matching basic part. They take two more loops. The CPU uses a Precision Mechanism and diamond; the PSU uses an Electron Tube and Sturdy Sheet.
retrocomputers.ponder.equipment.text_1: Start with an Equipment Frame: four planks, two iron sheets and an Andesite Casing. Add iron, tin, wiring and brass, then press and saw the chassis.
retrocomputers.ponder.equipment.text_2: Heat-mix glass, glowstone and silicon dust. Add a frame, a circuit board, an Electron Tube and wiring to the Phosphor Glass, then press it into four panels.
retrocomputers.ponder.equipment.text_3: Cut resin on a saw for keycaps. Add them, a stone button, a circuit board, wiring and solder to a frame. Finish it in the Press.
retrocomputers.ponder.equipment.text_4: Start the probe from a copper trace. Add polished rose quartz, resin, wiring, gold and solder, then press. Press R over equipment in JEI to see each line.
retrocomputers.ponder.assembly.text_1: Look through either open side of the chassis. The two shelves hold the four parts.
retrocomputers.ponder.assembly.text_2: Right-click the chassis with a CPU, RAM, drive and power supply to fill its four slots.
retrocomputers.ponder.assembly.text_3: Installing a new part returns the old one. A faster CPU runs commands sooner, and more RAM lets you type longer lines.
retrocomputers.ponder.assembly.text_4: A disk drive stores 128 KiB of files and 1024 lines of terminal history. A cassette drive stores 16 KiB and 768 lines.
retrocomputers.ponder.power.text_1: Put a Create Crafts & Additions Alternator against the chassis and drive it at 32 RPM or above.
retrocomputers.ponder.power.text_2: The base build draws 6 FE/t. A fully upgraded build draws 17 FE/t and needs the 32 FE/t power supply.
retrocomputers.ponder.power.text_3: The basic power supply supports up to 12 FE/t. Check the chassis status if the computer will not start.
retrocomputers.ponder.terminal.text_1: Build a filled rectangle, up to 50 by 50 panels. All panels must face the same way in the same plane.
retrocomputers.ponder.terminal.text_2: Right-click the computer with the probe to select it.
retrocomputers.ponder.terminal.text_3: Right-click the keyboard with the same probe.
retrocomputers.ponder.terminal.text_4: Click one panel to link the whole display. Keep the devices within 64 blocks of the computer and link again after resizing.
retrocomputers.ponder.terminal.text_5: Open the keyboard with a right-click. Type HELP and press Enter. Try INFO, ECHO HELLO and CLS.
retrocomputers.ponder.power.text_4: In Creative, connect a Creative Motor to the Alternator shaft for a quick test. Set the motor to 32 RPM or more.
retrocomputers.ponder.power.text_5: In survival, use a water wheel. A large cogwheel driving a small one doubles the speed. Repeat until a Speedometer shows at least 32 RPM.
retrocomputers.ponder.assembly.text_5: Right-click with an empty hand for status. Sneak and right-click with an empty hand to remove a part.
retrocomputers.ponder.terminal.text_6: The cables appear when you connect the devices. Look behind the chassis for the green monitor cable and the brown keyboard cable.
retrocomputers.ponder.mining.text_6: Run each tin ingot under a Mechanical Press to make a plate.
retrocomputers.ponder.boards.text_3: Compact two silicon dust and one quartz in a Basin under a Press. Smelt the blank and cut the ingot on a saw to get four wafers.
retrocomputers.ponder.boards.text_4: Start with ceramic on a Depot or Belt. Add a tin plate and a copper trace with Deployers, press the piece, then add solder with a Deployer.
retrocomputers.ponder.boards.text_5: Run that same four-step cycle twice to finish a circuit board. To make wiring harnesses, apply resin to a copper trace in a Deployer.

retrocomputers.terminal.help_files: Files: DIR TREE CD PWD MKDIR TOUCH WRITE APPEND CAT RM RMDIR DF
retrocomputers.terminal.help_paths: Use / for root and .. for parent. Names ignore case; spaces are not allowed.
retrocomputers.terminal.help_write: WRITE path text replaces a file; APPEND adds text. Use \n for a new line.
retrocomputers.terminal.help_scroll: Mouse wheel scrolls history. CAT reads files; TREE shows folders; DF shows free space.
retrocomputers.files.usage_df: DF / DISK / MEM: memory and disk usage
retrocomputers.ponder.files.text_1: Open the keyboard. Type MKDIR /notes and press Enter, then CD /notes to enter that folder. PWD shows your current folder.
retrocomputers.ponder.files.text_2: Type WRITE readme.txt Hello world to create a text file. CAT readme.txt reads it. APPEND readme.txt adds more text.
retrocomputers.ponder.files.text_3: DIR lists a folder, TREE / shows the whole disk. Scroll with the mouse wheel while the keyboard is open to read older output.
retrocomputers.ponder.files.text_4: Files live in mods/retrocomputers/computers/ followed by the computer name. Edit them in a text editor. DF shows the capacity: cassette 16 KiB, disk 128 KiB.
retrocomputers.ponder.files.text_5: RM removes a file; RMDIR removes an empty folder. CD / goes to the root. Use names without spaces. File names ignore case; text keeps its case.

retrocomputers.network.no_modem: ? Install a modem in the computer first

retrocomputers.network.missing: ? Module missing, unloaded or linked to another computer
retrocomputers.terminal.help_network: Hardware: PORTS, READ m1, SET m1 0..15, UNLINK m1. A modem is required.
retrocomputers.ponder.modules.text_1: Install a Wired Modem by right-clicking the chassis. The computer works without it, but external modules require one.
retrocomputers.ponder.modules.text_2: Place an Interface Module on the face of a block. Select the computer with the Linking Probe, then click the module. Each module gets a name such as m1.
retrocomputers.ponder.modules.text_3: Type PORTS to list modules and READ m1 to read its block. Depending on the block, you see redstone, Create RPM, item counts and tank contents.
retrocomputers.ponder.modules.text_4: SET m1 15 outputs redstone from the module. SET m1 0 switches it off. Use a lamp, a clutch or a gearshift to control machines.
retrocomputers.ponder.modules.text_5: Blue cables show the module connections. Spark traces appear when linking. UNLINK m1 disconnects a module. Removing the modem disables its outputs.
terminal.name_prompt: FIRST START: enter a computer name (1–32 letters, digits, _ or -), then Enter. Example: lab

terminal.python_example: Try RUN /hello.py. NAME new_name renames this PC and its folder.

python.stop_before_name: Use STOP before renaming the computer.
python.slots: Four Python programs are already running. Stop one first.
retrocomputers.ponder.python.header: Naming a computer and running Python
retrocomputers.ponder.python.text_1: At the first boot enter a name, for example lab. The name stays with this computer. NAME new_name renames it later.
retrocomputers.ponder.python.text_2: Open mods/retrocomputers/computers/lab in your real Minecraft folder. Each computer has its own folder. Old files are migrated here after naming.
retrocomputers.ponder.python.text_3: EXAMPLES creates Python, Lua, C, C++, C#, Java and Rust samples. NANO /examples/hello.lua opens the editor. Ctrl+S saves, Ctrl+X exits, F5 saves and runs.
retrocomputers.ponder.python.text_4: In Python use import computer. computer.read('m1') returns block data; computer.set('m1', 15) outputs redstone. A modem and linked module are required.
retrocomputers.ponder.python.text_5: RUN file selects a language by extension. LANGS lists available toolchains. Ctrl+C stops execution. Programs accept keyboard input and save files in the PC folder.
